name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+30 district lean with a well-funded incumbent
Raskin has raised $7.4M vs. under $17K for Riley
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal a race
model.rationale: Raskin holds a D+30 seat with a massive financial advantage and markets price his win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe D with a margin near the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen incumbent scandal or collapse in Democratic turnout could narrow the margin meaningfully.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jamie Raskin seeks another term in a Maryland district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan baseline near D+30. He enters the general election after easily securing renomination, facing Republican Cheryl Riley and a Green Party candidate with little visible support.

The resource gap is stark: Raskin has raised over $7.4 million and holds $7.9 million on hand, while Riley has raised about $17,000. No independent spending, polling, or expert ratings point to a competitive race, and prediction markets price Raskin's chances near 97%. The forecast treats this as a Safe Democratic hold with a margin in the low thirties.
